name: banner-compare
label: The ENEMY DELETED banner, real ROM above and this build below: 0 pixels over all 58 frames. The banner is text -- a font of 8x16 cells and a record per message, twenty cells uploaded as five 32x16 objects -- and all forty-five of the game's messages are in the build. The unrolling is one shared affine matrix whose vertical scale opens from a flat line, overshoots into a stretch, holds and rolls back up.

name: battle-open-compare
label: How a battle opens, real ROM above and this build below. Found with the harness's first save state at a battle's FIRST frame, which immediately showed two things wrong here: a battle OPENS with the chip window (frame 165, unprompted) where this build made you wait 1260 frames for it, and BATTLE START! follows the chip window rather than the intro. Corrected, the banner lands at 291 against the real ROM's 292.

name: bugbomb-compare
label: BugBomb, real ROM left and this build right: 0.0 pixels a frame over seventy. Its arc used to be swept and was one rounding step out on the frame before it lands; the constants are now read out of the object while it is in the air -- vx 0x2C000, vz 0x26062, gravity 0x2800 over 42 frames.

name: cursor-compare
label: The chip window's cursor walking five slots, real ROM left and this build right: 170 frames, 0 pixels. Two one-frame bugs, neither of them the cursor delay it had been blamed on -- the card's palette landing a frame before its tiles, and the bracket's blink flipping a frame early. Neither was findable until the fixture could run the same script on both sides.

name: full-battle-loop
label: A whole battle end to end in the rollup ROM: the chip window a battle opens with, the BATTLE START! ribbon, the fight, the win, the RESULT window with its reward, and into the next battle's chip select. This loop did not exist before today -- the release build fielded four enemies that delete the navi in fifteen seconds and started the custom gauge empty, 1260 frames before the first chip. Every piece here is separately matched to the real ROM pixel for pixel.

name: vdoll-compare
label: VDoll, real ROM left and this build right: 0.0 pixels a frame over seventy. The doll rises to the top of the screen and stands where it lands. Its launch is vx 0x1EEEE, vz 0x2F333, gravity 0x2000 over sixty frames -- and unlike a bomb it MOVES AND THEN FALLS, which was the last pixel.

name: wave-departure-compare
label: The Mettaur's shockwave, real ROM left and this build right. A hop is not one sprite moving: the real ROM spawns a whole new segment on the next panel and the old one stops where it is, playing out its own animation until it comes back round to its last frame. The residue had been recorded as the virus holding its pickaxe too long -- its body is 0 pixels across all 70 frames.
